goal.source_text: Maximize this rocket fin's stability, keep drag low, keep it under 40 g, must fit a 3-inch body tube.

constraints.label: Fin set must fit within 3-inch (76.2 mm) body tube diameter

assumptions: The 40 g limit applies to the total mass of all fins, since the goal does not say per fin.
Stability is targeted at about 2.5 calibers rather than maximized, to avoid weathercocking above about 3 calibers.
The 3-inch body tube fit is interpreted as a root chord no longer than the 76.2 mm body diameter, the closest available dimension constraint.
Design velocity of 120 m/s is taken from the context block since the goal does not state a speed.
Edge profile pinned to 'rounded' for this recording: the Part Studio's edge_profile input is still pending.

Agent found a feasible 3-fin design under 40 g, narrowly ahead of CMA-ES.
message.body:
Starting from an infeasible seed (59.717 g, root_chord violation, aggregate -0.2763), the agent cut root_chord from 90.0 to 61.0, raised semi_span from 60.0 to 69.5, widened taper_ratio from 0.5 to 0.75, lowered sweep from 30 to 22 deg, and dropped from 4 fins to 3. This brought fin mass to 39.614 g, under the 40 g limit, and cut drag from 1.61 N to 1.318 N, while stability moved from 2.232 to 2.122 cal, slightly further from the 2.5 cal target but still within tolerance. Physically, fewer and less-chorded fins cut wetted area and mass, and the longer span recovers much of the lost stabilizing lift. The agent's aggregate of 0.6999 is only marginally above CMA-ES at 0.6893, so the gap is small and could be noise given a single run at 64 evaluations. CMA-ES actually reached lower drag (1.271 N) and much lower mass (31.321 g), with the agent ahead mainly through stability closer to target (2.122 vs 2.061 cal). Random search stayed infeasible at -0.0025.
